I did not re-run the change from scratch; I attacked the load-bearing claims and the prior gate.

**Attacks and outcomes**

1. *"Every insertion point escaped"* — I enumerated every string interpolation inside `chart()`/`hero()` (`sed -n 119,240p bench/report.py | grep '{'`). Only `title`, `subtitle`, panel `name`, `LABELS.get(b,b)`, `value`, `note`, `figure`, `unit_text`, `line`, `fmt(...)` and the two `aria-label` values are strings; each is wrapped in `xml_text`/`xml_attr`, and every other interpolation is a number, `FONT`, or a theme colour. Claim holds.

2. *"The tests would notice a lost escaping"* — I built a mutation harness on an isolated copy (`/tmp/mut`, real tree untouched) removing escaping one site at a time. `panel_name`, `chart_aria`, `hero_title`, `hero_subtitle`, `hero_line`, `hero_tile_name`, `hero_build_label` each turn the suite red. Survivors: `chart_value`, `chart_note`, `hero_figure`, `hero_unit`, `hero_bar_figure` — all fed by `fmt()`/`ratio_text()`, which emit only numbers plus a literal unit (`fmt` at report.py:75-87), so no dataset string can reach them today. That is untested defence-in-depth, not an open injection path → advisory, not blocking. My first harness showed false survivors from stale `__pycache__`; re-run with bytecode cleared, `hero_line` is caught (`ParseError: not well-formed (invalid token): line 7, column 93`).

3. *"Dataset-driven injection is closed, not just `--label`"* — independent synthetic corpus with `</text><script>alert(1)</script>` as a build id and as a `pauses.jsonl` step key: 10 charts, all parse, `raw_script_literal=0` everywhere, payload present as text in the plugins and memory charts (the two charts that draw dataset ids). Claim holds.

4. *"Byte-identical ordinary output"* — the `/tmp/aud-head/bench/report.py` baseline hashes to `git show HEAD:bench/report.py` (`53ad2ea7…`), so it is not a doctored baseline; `diff -r` on the 10 SVGs and the Markdown stdout were clean.
